verdict.rationale: Fedora Workstation ships its own isolation tools: Boxes for virtual machines, built-in container tools, and a Container_Toolbox subvariant. A user can use these to stand up a separate environment for testing instead of working on the host. This is genuine sandbox isolation, not a dry-run, but the docs never describe it as a way to keep testing apart from production data or for agent-driven testing. Missing for 10: explicit docs on isolating test workloads from real or production data, guidance on agent or AI testing workflows, and independent hands-on corroboration of using Boxes or Toolbox as a test sandbox.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Boxes takes the guesswork out of using virtual machines.
High-efficiency tools for creating, running and managing containers
